title: Recycle handoff at the DEC-38 / WCLI-51 boundary
description:
Written after the recycler fresh request, as ordered, following the WCLI-47 precedent for this repository.

WHAT THIS SESSION LANDED, all measured on the refs rather than remembered.
- WCLI-50 filed, the skill hardening content half, opum-ai/ward-cli#96.
- WCLI-48 and WCLI-49 closed as moot under DEC-38, WCLI-50 corrected and WCLI-51 filed, #97.
- The eval format coordination with opum-fleet recorded on WCLI-50, #98.
- WCLI-51 implemented, independently reviewed and landed, #99. Then WCLI-51 closed and WCLI-53 filed, #101.
- DEC-38 option A promoted: origin/main and origin/dev were both 61aa8a24 when I read them back, after a verified fast-forward pushed as origin/dev:main. main measured 0 rules, so nothing was configured to wait on there.

STATE AT HANDOVER. dev is db0e3be and is +1 against origin/main, the #101 close-out, tracker-only. That is deliberate and matches the shape the previous session left; it is available for the next promotion rather than being a gap. Tree clean, nothing unpushed, 0 open PRs. Tracker 53 records, 36 Done, 17 To Do, none In Progress. Local branches dev and main only.

THE ONE THING WORTH CARRYING, because it cost real time and its correction is now in two other repositories. My DEC-38 decision packet asserted that the reporting path handling of vault_format_unsupported would be unreachable once the state document version gate went. It was asserted, not measured, and it was false: parseVaultState still raises that code for a stored profile approval whose snapshotVersion differs, a site DEC-38 keeps. Implemented as packeted, ward doctor and ward status each exited 6 with EMPTY stdout, breaking ADR 0007 contract that doctor always reports all five checks. Caught by the independent reviewer, fixed, and pinned by a test measured failing against the unfixed source first. opum-agent corrected DEC-38 record at 87442f3 and opum-doc was told. AC3 on WCLI-51 was amended rather than checked, because as filed it required the deletion the review disproved.

SUCCESSOR NEXT WORK, in order.
1. WCLI-50, skill hardening. It is the content half and it is NOT started. The format is settled and recorded on the task: option (a), Ward cases live here, run against the ward plugin, and a ward-cli scripts/run-eval.sh is the ship gate. opum-fleet holds the distribution half as OFLE-162 and asked to be pinged with the plugin entry name and ref when the content half is close.
2. WCLI-52, the backup residual the review found untracked.
3. WCLI-53, the CI flake. Its mechanism was filed fleet-wide by opum-agent, so other repositories are being checked for the same shape.

TWO THINGS NOT TO RE-DERIVE. The CI flake is real and measured three ways, not a flake to be retried away: test/key-provider.test.ts:293 asserts wall-clock elapsed under 400ms and it failed at 474ms on the pull_request workflow for 61aa8a24 while the push workflow for the SAME SHA passed, the two overlapping by 26 seconds on one runner group. And the quest task complete exit-5 I saw while the write landed correctly is still unreproduced; the write did land both times, verified by reading the records rather than the exit code or the JSON, so treat it as noise until someone reproduces it.
finalSummary:
The recycler asked for a handoff written after its request, as the WCLI-47 precedent has it, and this record is that handoff. It carries no acceptance criteria because it is a note rather than work: the reasoning is in the description above, and it is deliberately a summary of what landed plus a pointer to the three tasks that carry the forward work, not a second copy of them.

Written after the opum-workflow flush had already run in write mode. That flush wrote .claude/handovers/cursor.md naming version 0.11.0, and wrote NO tracker note, correctly: no task was In Progress at the time, and the tree was clean with nothing unpushed, which are two of the three documented reasons the flush stays silent. Both are the designed behaviour rather than a fault, and the cursor was read back to confirm it exists and names its writer.

The cursor itself cannot be committed: .claude/handovers/ is in this repository .gitignore, so the flush output is deliberately machine-local and the successor reads it through the SessionStart injection rather than from a ref. That is why the durable half of this handoff is a tracker record at all.

Nothing was left In Progress. WCLI-54 is closed by the same change that lands it.
